triggers: a threadgroup-staged Metal GEMM is slower than expected despite fully coalesced global reads

payload.goal: Choose staging topology by measurement, not by CUDA coalescing intuition.

problem.statement: CUDA-style reasoning says global loads must coalesce. On Apple unified memory, a 32-iteration coalesced A-staging loop (thread owns a k-column) ran ~30ms while an 8-iteration non-coalesced loop (thread owns a row) ran ~13.3ms on the same 32x32-tile q4 kernel: the extra serialized staging iterations dominated, and L2 absorbed the strided reads.

payload.technique: fewer staging iterations beat coalesced staging; L2 absorbs non-coalesced global reads
payload.what: Threadgroup-staged GEMM kernels on M-series GPUs, especially with k-steps of 8 or 16 where a coalesced mapping needs one loop iteration per tile row.
payload.when: Benchmark both staging topologies under ABBA alternation (A/B/B/A blocks, median per block) before committing to one; keep the loop with fewer iterations unless measurement contradicts it. Record the decision in the candidate evidence.
how: unified-memory L2 behavior differs by chip generation; re-measure per target before generalizing

raw.seed: onyx-infer kernel-agent/q4-mma episode, ABBA-measured on Apple M5 Max (Mac17,14, Metal 4, metalfe-32023.921.6), 2026-11-17
